title: i deleted my bot's babysitter and replayed 10 trades without it. +2.25R vs +2.22R.
author: luwihu
selftext:
So my bot has a babysitter and it turns out the babysitter does nothing.

Quick background so this makes sense. 4h MACD on hyperliquid, seven assets, take profit sits at exactly 1x the placed stop distance, so every trade is basically +1R or -1R by construction. On top of that there's a monitor goal that wakes up every four hours and can kill a position early for three reasons. Been open too long, adx dropped, or a trailing profit lock got tripped.

I built that thing carefully. It is the most defensive part of the whole setup. And last week's review told me 57 percent of my exits were coming from it rather than from the trade's own stop or target, which felt like a lot but also felt fine, because that's what a safety net is for. Right?

Then i actually measured it.

Here's the bit you can steal, and it costs you nothing. Hyperliquid's info API is public. No key, no signature, no login, you just POST a wallet address at it:

python

    import requests
    r = requests.post("https://api.hyperliquid.xyz/info",
                      json={"type":"userFills","user":"0xYOURWALLET"})

That gives you every fill the wallet has ever made, with the realised pnl on each one. `historicalOrders` gives you the stop levels that were actually resting. `candleSnapshot` gives you 5 minute candles for any window you want. Which means you can take any closed trade you've ever made and replay it forward as if none of your exit logic existed. First touch of +1R or -1R wins, cap it at your max hold, done.

So i did that for all ten trades since the take profit change.

with the monitor: +2.22R without it: +2.25R

Ten trades is nothing and i know it, so don't take the number, take the method. But the composition is what actually got me. It spoiled two winners and it rescued two losers. Coin flip.

The trailing lock was the worst of the three rules and the reason is dumb. I built the ratchet back when my target was 2.5R, when a winner had real room to run and something worth protecting. Then in July i measured where trades actually peak on this strategy, found they mostly top out well under 1R, and moved the target down to 1.0R. Never went back and deleted the ratchet.

Under a 1R target there is no room between "in profit" and "at target" for a trailing stop to live in! Anything that moves far enough to trip a rung is already sitting at the exit. So all it can do is stop you out on the retrace. Which it did, on a ZEC short, at breakeven, and on the candles that trade went on and touched its full take profit an hour later. A whole R from one vestigial rule :)

That monitor was costing about 200 credits a day, roughly 70 percent of the bot's entire compute bill, to produce minus 0.03R.

If you're running agents on hyperliquid, go replay your own exits before you trust another one of your agent's summaries. Four lines of python and half an hour.

Has anyone here actually measured what their exit rules do, rather than what they were designed to do?

comments.author: ConsiderationNo9952
comments.body: can you use mae mfe stats for similar analysis?

replies.author: luwihu
replies.body:
yeah i did exactly that first, and it pointed me the wrong way, which is the interesting part.

mfe/mae by exit type over the same ten trades:

take profit (n=3): realised +1.04R, mfe +1.15R  
stop (n=2): realised -1.01R, mfe +0.26R  
monitor (n=5): realised +0.22R, mfe +0.59R, so 0.36R given back each

read that on its own and the answer is obvious. take partial profit at 1R, let the rest run. so i tested it. worth +0.14R across all ten. noise. because only 4 of the 10 trades ever touched 1.0R mfe, and three of those four already took their take profit right there. the trades doing the giving back never got near 1R, they topped out at 0.59.

so mfe tells you what was available on the path. it does not tell you what your rule would have done instead of the rule you ran. for that you need the forward replay, same entry, same stop, first touch wins, rule deleted.

where mfe absolutely is the right tool: picking the target in the first place. mine sat at 2.5R while measured mfe peaked around 0.4 to 0.7R. geometrically unreachable. moving it to 1.0R is the single change that made the thing profitable, and that was pure mfe, no replay needed.
